title: Sharabhanga
hook: a king of the gods is visiting an old sage, and when Rama walks up, the god leaves

segments.voice: Yesterday: the enemy becomes the guide. Viradha rose free from the pit, a cursed musician released, and sent the brothers to a sage.

Rama follows Viradha's directions, and near Sharabhanga's hermitage he stops. There's a chariot in the air above the clearing, blazing like the sun, pulled by green horses. A white umbrella shades the figure in it, and attendants crowd around. That's Indra, Rama tells Lakshmana, king of the gods, talking with the sage. And as the brothers walk closer, Indra says something to his companions, and the chariot rises and goes.
screen: `A CHARIOT ABOVE THE CLEARING.` → `INDRA, KING OF THE GODS.` → `HE LEAVES AS RAMA COMES.`

segments.voice: Why does Indra leave? Valmiki gives a reason, spoken to the people around him. Rama is coming, and I shouldn't meet him yet. He has work to do first. When it's done, I'll see him. The text hints at what lies ahead, a war the gods themselves need Rama to fight, but says no more. The point is the picture: the god of storms and rain stepping aside for a man in bark clothes. Rama goes in, and the very old sage welcomes him. Indra came to take me to Brahma's world, Sharabhanga says. I've earned it by my austerities. But I heard you were near, and I wouldn't leave until I had seen my guest. Then the old sage makes an extraordinary offer. All the worlds I've won by my tapas, all that merit, I give to you. Take it. Rama says no, kindly. I'll earn my own worlds. Just tell me where in this forest I should live. A free gift of heaven, from someone who means it, and Rama turns it down, not out of pride but because he has his own road to walk. Sharabhanga accepts that, and points him to Sutikshna, another sage further on. But first he asks Rama to stay a little longer and watch. He has one last thing to do.
screen: `I SHOULDN'T MEET HIM YET.` · `I WAITED TO SEE MY GUEST.` · `TAKE ALL MY MERIT.` · `I'LL EARN MY OWN WORLDS.` · then, large: `A GIFT OF HEAVEN, DECLINED.`

segments.voice: Rest your hands open on your knees and think of something you're slowly working toward, a skill, a habit, a repair in a relationship. Picture yourself taking the next small step on your own feet, and feel your own weight on the seat, carrying you, as you breathe.
Sharabhanga. The old sage who waited to see Rama before going to heaven, and offered him all his merit, which Rama kindly declined.
Your line: I'll earn my own worlds. Rama wants his own road, not a shortcut. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: In the text, Indra withdraws before meeting Rama, and some devotees read the scene as the gods waiting on Rama's mission.

original.note: Sanskrit śarabhaṅga: the name of the old sage of Dandaka who waits to see Rama.

trapdoor: what you thought: the sage is just one more hermit on the way.
what it means: he has delayed heaven itself to see Rama, and offers it to him.
what a scholar hears: Aranya 5 has Indra withdraw because Rama's task isn't done, an early hint of the war the gods are waiting for.
recall: the sage who tells Valmiki Rama's story

chat.says: Why would Rama turn down a sage's gift of all his heavenly merit?
options: He wanted to earn his own worlds and walk his own road, not out of pride.
He didn't believe the sage really had any merit to give him away.

chat.meaning: Sharabhanga offered Rama all the worlds his tapas had won. Rama kindly declined: I'll earn my own worlds, and asked only where to live.

Sharabhanga.meaning: an old sage of Dandaka who waited to see Rama

Indra.meaning: king of the gods, god of storms and rain

Brahma.meaning: the creator god; his world is the sage's goal
